quote: We've always relied on NOAA from their official observation sites. My worry is the longer that this goes lapsed, the more likely that we lose that data forever, that's unrecoverable. That's 150 years of science. You're starting over.
name: Jacob Lanier
title: Meteorologist, FOX4

quote: To suddenly say, 'We can't adequately assess the drought situation anymore' because we've lost the data that we look at weekly to make these assessments, that's unacceptable.
name: Matthew Sittel
title: Assistant State Climatologist, Kansas State University

quote: It's tough. Do we lose these products for a week, for a month, for a year, forever? Nobody knows.
name: Matthew Sittel
title: Assistant State Climatologist, Kansas State University

quote: I think the impacts are going to be pretty widespread. The weather data is still out there, but it's just going to get that much harder to access at this point.

quote: This is your taxpayer money that you're not getting full benefit of right now.
name: Eric Hunt

quote: The cuts would take us back to the 1950s in terms of our scientific footing and the American people.
name: Craig McLean

quote: When you cut the research, you cut the ability to improve the forecasts and the predictions. It's not just hurricanes or tornadoes. The climate side of things includes seasonal outlook. quote: The proposed closure of OAR and weather and climate labs would deny Americans the vital weather data they need to protect their lives and property, especially during natural disasters... The elimination of NOAA's critical weather and climate data would devastate the agricultural industry, which relies on reliable and free access to NOAA data to plan crops.
name: Rep. Gabe Amo et al.
title: Ranking Member, House Subcommittee on Environment
publication: Letter to Secretary Howard Lutnick and Acting Administrator Laura Grimm

quote: Without NOAA research, National Weather Service (NWS) weather models and products will stagnate, observational data collection will be reduced, public outreach will decrease... title: In partnership with the National Weather Association
publication: Stand Up for NOAA Research – The Time to Act is Now
